properties.decision: PROPOSED IDEA, not a commitment: give the agent a lookup from a FILE (or symbol) to the Decisions, Requirements and Constraints that govern it — "what does the design already say about the code I am about to change?" — resolved by traversal rather than by keyword search.
properties.name: IDEA — an agent about to edit a file can ask what the design already decided about it, without guessing search terms
properties.rationale:
RECORDED UNDER ANTHONY'S 2026-08-08 TEST PROTOCOL: run a task as if reflow2 did not exist, then run it leaning on reflow2, compare, and propose what would have helped. His stated aim, quoted so it is not lost: he is NOT trying to change how the agent functions, but to make available skills/tools that make the agent's job easier and better. This idea is scoped to that.

THE EVIDENCE IS TWO FIXES DONE THE SAME DAY, WITH DIFFERENT AMOUNTS OF REFLOW2.

(1) THE DUPLICATES/MERGE FIX — reflow2 CHANGED THE OUTCOME, and the whole difference was one call. dev_storyflow reported merge candidates scoring 81-85 on unrelated nodes. Read as a code problem, the obvious fix is 'the scorer is bad, raise the threshold' — a plausible, shippable, WRONG fix. A `search_design` for 'duplicate merge similarity' returned `dec:ask-not-repair` as the top hit, and that decision reframed the entire task: possible_duplicate is a DETECT gap, HEAL merges only on a human-drawn edge, a heuristic must not drive it. The bug was not a bad threshold; it was an ACCEPTED DECISION DEFEATED BY THE BUILD, and the correct fix (mark the edge's basis, re-route suspicions to the gap layer) is not reachable from the code alone. Without reflow2 this session ships a threshold bump and the design stays quietly violated.

(2) THE CLAIM-LIVENESS FIX — reflow2 helped at the FRAMING and not at all at the SOLUTION. The graph supplied the finding that mattered (`cap:claim-liveness` was status `verified` while its central claim was false under `--shared`) and `propagate_change` named exactly what to touch, including three Verifications that would be invalidated. But the fix itself — an RAII seat lease, and then a two-set registry after the first design proved unsafe — came entirely from reading code and from a FAILING TEST. No reflow2 detector had anything to say about it. Worth stating plainly rather than overclaiming: the two-set flaw was caught by `cargo test`, not by the design brain.

THE GENERALISATION, and it is the actionable part: REFLOW2'S LEVERAGE IS AT PROBLEM FRAMING AND BLAST RADIUS, NOT AT SOLUTION DESIGN. That is not a weakness — it is where a design brain SHOULD have leverage, and it argues for investing there rather than trying to help write the patch.

SO WHAT IS MISSING, CONCRETELY: in case (1) the decision was found because a lucky choice of search words hit it. `search_design` is BM25 over node text, so the agent must already suspect what it is looking for. AN AGENT ABOUT TO EDIT `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs` SHOULD BE ABLE TO ASK WHAT GOVERNS THAT FILE AND BE TOLD `dec:ask-not-repair`, WITHOUT KNOWING THE WORD 'DUPLICATE'. The graph already holds every hop needed: `art:heal` REALIZES `cap:heal`, which is GOVERNED_BY the decisions that constrain it, SATISFIES the requirements behind it, and is VERIFIED by the checks that would break. That is a traversal from a path to its governing intent, and today there is no tool for it — `propagate_change` is the closest but needs a recorded ChangeEvent and answers 'what does this touch', not 'what was already decided here'.

WHY THIS FITS THE STATED AIM: it changes nothing about how the agent works. It is a lookup the agent chooses to make at the moment it is already opening a file, and it answers the one question a stateless agent cannot answer for itself and does not know to ask.

CANDIDATE SHAPES, none chosen: (a) a `governs` tool taking a path or symbol, returning Decisions/Requirements/Constraints/Verifications reachable from the Artifact at that location, ranked by hop distance; (b) the same as a skill that runs before an edit, the read-side sibling of impact-check; (c) cheapest of all and worth pricing first — have `link_artifact`/`reconcile_artifacts` responses already carry the governing decisions for the artifact named, since the traversal is the same and the agent is already there.

OPEN QUESTIONS THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether path-level granularity is enough (a 1,700-line file may be governed by decisions relevant to only one of its functions); whether an unregistered file — one with no Artifact — should answer 'nothing governs this' or 'this file is not in the design', which are very different statements and the second is the honest one; and whether ranking by hop distance is meaningful or merely plausible.
